listings.title: Old Fashioned Farm Estate Sale
listings.description: * Sale Postponed to Next Weekend 10/3 - 10/4 Due to Weather - See You Then! 🤠* We are always hunting for old farms frozen in time... this is one of those special treasure hunts! *UPDATE 9/24 - Native American artifacts were uncovered hidden deep in a closet! These were found decades ago on the grounds of the farm, within the cow fields. More photos of the Ware chairs, record collection, and Ford 8n Tractor. *UPDATE 9/23 - MORE PHOTOS ADDED* This century old dairy farm has fresh, multigenerational, and regionally made treasure to uncover including primitives, tools, decoration, furniture, and more dating back to the 1800's. Ford Gas 1948 8N Tractor with Loader - Starts Up & Runs Perfect Hit & Miss Engine, Vintage Gas Pumps, Primitive Shaker Style Ware Chairs , Early American Pine Primitive Corner Cabinet Primitive decor, Good Tools, Heavy Farm Bolts & Hardware, Gas Pumps, Antique Books, Retro Glassware, Mahogany Corner Cabinet, Early Arm & Hammer Anvil, Tons of Tins, Primitive Ice Harvesting Tools, Antique Wooden Boxes, Farm Bolts & Goods, Cattle Panels, 70's GMC Farm Truck Parts, ...and much more as we uncover this estate! The Ware chairs & corner cabinet have been on the property and a piece of Gloucester County history for 150 years! A brief history of the Ware Chairs: Ware chairs were made between 1800 and 1940 by five generations of a family in the Cumberland County community of Roadstown, northwest of Bridgeton. The patriarch, Maskell Ware, found a niche in the furniture market by turning out rocking chairs. Subsequent Ware chairs were characterized by slat backs, woven-rush seats and uprights, and stretchers turned on a lathe. More photos & details on the tractor to come. We update our listings usually daily before sales, check back regularly. Add us on Facebook to get all of the information first: Facebook.com/AuctionsByMesiano
